Coinbase Launches Fixed-Rate Crypto-Backed Loans Powered by Morpho Midnight
summary:
Morpho, the blockchain-based network for digital asset credit markets, today announced that Coinbase has launched fixed-rate, fixed-maturity crypto-backed loans powered by Morpho Midnight.
The launch marks the first enterprise-scale integration of Morpho Midnight, shortly after the protocol’s debut, bringing fixed-rate onchain credit directly to users through the Coinbase app. Coinbase users can now borrow USDC against their BTC, with their borrowing rate and repayment date fixed from the outset. The move takes onchain borrowing beyond the predominantly variable-rate model, giving users greater certainty over the cost and duration of their borrowing.
The new product sits alongside Coinbase’s existing Morpho-powered variable-rate loans, which have grown to more than $1.4 billion in active loans backed by approximately $3 billion of collateral. Users can now choose between the flexibility of variable-rate borrowing and the predictability of a fixed rate and defined maturity.
This integration expands Coinbase’s existing use of Morpho. Coinbase retains control of the user experience, while Morpho provides the underlying credit infrastructure and Base acts as the settlement layer.
“Fixed rates and defined maturities are fundamental to how credit markets work, and bringing them to a platform at Coinbase’s scale is an important step for onchain lending,” said Paul Frambot, CEO and co-founder of Morpho. “What is particularly significant is how quickly Coinbase has been able to build on Midnight. It shows that fintechs can use open infrastructure to launch sophisticated credit products without having to recreate the underlying credit stack themselves.”
“Coinbase Borrow gives our customers access to liquidity without having to sell their assets, and fixed-rate borrowing gives them even greater choice over how they manage that credit,” said Jacob Frantz, Yield & Investments product lead at Coinbase. “By adding fixed rates and defined maturities alongside our existing variable-rate offering, customers can choose the structure that best fits their needs while continuing to access borrowing directly through Coinbase.”
Morpho Midnight enables lenders and borrowers to set defined rates and maturities, with loans executed onchain through market-based pricing. The protocol is designed to support a broader range of credit products, including crypto-backed lending, structured credit and financing backed by tokenised real-world assets.

Revenue Increases by Over 50% as iwoca Launches New Products to Solve More SME Problems
summary:
iwoca reveals a record year of growth and lending in 2025, and announces an expansion of services in new areas to provide SMEs with a range of products to help them understand, access and manage credit.
Providing tech-led decisions to help SMEs grow
iwoca’s financial accounts show revenue increased by 56% to £366 million in 2025, up from £234 million the previous year. Across its markets in the UK and Germany, the company provided £1.5 billion in funding, rising from £952 million in 2024, across ~100,000 SME loans funded in 2025. iwoca has now lent over £6 billion to small businesses since 2012.
The growth in lending is powered by iwoca’s proprietary technology, data-driven approach, and market-leading customer experience. Productivity improvements alongside growth at scale, helped to increase profits to £85.1 million in 2025. 
Building products to help SMEs solve problems
iwoca is reinvesting these profits into solving more problems for SMEs. The company today announces the launch of its Business Credit Card, which will give UK SMEs access to flexible credit for day-to-day spending and unexpected costs. 
This follows the launch of Credit Compass earlier this year - a free tool designed to give every UK SME clear insight into their business’s credit standing, and iwocaPay in 2020 - a B2B BNPL service which gives businesses and their customers greater flexibility over payment terms. Over 10,000 SMEs have registered with Credit Compass, giving them insights into their financial status, tools to improve their credit health and expanded access to credit. iwocaPay has processed £100 million of payments for 13,000 firms - the vast majority of whom have annual revenue of less than £500,000, meaning thousands of small businesses are accessing trade credit for the first time. iwoca is set to launch further products over the coming months in insurance and M&A to give SMEs more tools to address the challenges they face. 
Alongside these new products, iwoca has ambitious plans to continue growing its lending business. The company recently closed a new £250 million facility with a leading UK bank and WAM Capital. iwoca’s lending capabilities are also boosted by over 50 partnerships which give SMEs access to finance through platforms they regularly use, including Starling, Tide, Monzo and xero. 
Christoph Rieche, iwoca’s CEO and co-founder said: “Since launch in 2012, we've focused relentlessly on our mission to finance underserved SMEs. While we’re now lending at scale, and announcing new products and partnerships, the funding gap continues to widen. We have more work to do.”
iwoca’s recent growth and the development of new products led it to win Fintech Company of the Year 2026 at the Fintech Awards London.

Capital.com Launches Stocks and ETF Investing Across Europe
summary:
Capital.com, the global online trading platform, today announced its next step toward becoming a multi-asset trading and investment platform, with direct investing in stocks and exchange-traded funds (ETFs) now available to clients across its European markets. The move extends the platform beyond short-term trading to include long-term investing.
The launch reflects a broader view of how clients approach markets. Some come to the platform to act on a short-term view, while others are building a position they intend to hold for years. Built for Better Decisions, the principle behind Capital.com's platform, is about matching the instrument to the client's intention, rather than expecting one type of instrument to serve every purpose. Direct ownership of stocks and ETFs gives clients investing for the long term a product built for that, sitting alongside the short-term trading instruments already on the platform.
The offering spans more than 2,280 stocks and ETFs across US and European markets, including a broad range of local European companies. There is no commission on stock or ETF investments. Stocks and ETFs are available to eligible clients across nearly all of Capital.com's European Economic Area markets.*
As with the rest of its product range, Capital.com offers stocks and ETFs on an execution-only, non-advised basis and does not recommend which stocks or ETFs to buy. Clients can access stocks and ETFs following Capital.com’s standard onboarding process for new products. Client assets are held under the safeguarding arrangements that apply across Capital.com's regulated entities.
Commenting on the launch, Christoforos Soutzis, CEO Europe, Capital.com, said:
“Across Europe, clients rarely fit into a single category. Many trade on short-term views and build long-term positions within the same week. A platform built for only one side of that no longer matches how people actually invest. That is why we decided to expand our offering and become a multi-asset provider, giving clients across Europe a genuine choice between the two, in one place.”
More broadly, the move reflects Capital.com's ambition to serve a wider range of client needs, from traders acting on short-term views to investors building long-term positions, within a single multi-asset platform, without changing what the platform stands for.
Commenting on the launch, Sasha Gubochkin, Chief Product Officer, Capital.com, said:
“Every product we add to the platform, both on web and app, has to answer the same question. Does it help a client understand their situation more clearly before they act? Stocks and ETFs are the latest expression of that commitment. As Capital.com grows to serve more of what clients need, from short-term trading to long-term investing, the design principles stay the same, with less noise, less urgency, and information presented clearly enough that the decision belongs to the client.”
Stocks and ETFs sit alongside the research, charting and portfolio tools already built into Capital.com's platform, so clients can apply the same standard of information to a long-term holding as they would to a short-term position.
Europe is first in line for the new offering. Stocks and ETFs will be rolled out across Capital.com's other markets, including the UAE and the UK, in the coming months, reflecting Capital.com's continued commitment to serve clients across the full range of how they engage with markets.

summary:

Customers can now apply for a Sainsbury’s Personal Loan, powered by NatWest Boxed, through the Sainsbury’s Money website. Whether it is buying a car or improving a home, the loans offer practical support for customers planning their next step. while members of Nectar, the UK’s largest loyalty programme with more than 24 million members, can epresentative 6.3% APR by providing their Nectar card number*. 
An instant access savings account will follow in October. Designed for customers who want their money to work harder without tying it up, it will allow deposits and withdrawals at any time, with no penalty for taking money out. The rate, which will be confirmed at launch, will be competitive and even better for Nectar members. 
Today's announcement follows the launch of Sainsbury's Money in July 2026 and the completion of the Sainsbury's Bank transformation. Sainsbury's set out a new direction for its financial services business in 2024, and Sainsbury's Money now works with specialist partners to bring customers simple, competitive products, rather than operating a bank itself. Personal loans and savings are the first products to reach customers under that model.
Andrew Ellis, CEO of NatWest Boxed, said:
“This partnership brings together Sainsbury’s Money’s understanding of its customers with our banking expertise and technology. NatWest Boxed provides the platform, banking capability and operational support behind the scenes, so customers can apply for a loan or open a savings account through the Sainsbury’s Money experience they already know and trust.” 
Patrick Short, Managing Director of Financial Services at Sainsbury's, said:
“Sainsbury's Money is about offering our customers straightforward products that are built around what they actually need, with the extra value they already expect from Nectar. Working with NatWest Boxed brings together their banking expertise and our understanding of our customers, so we can offer genuinely competitive products, with an even better rate for our Nectar members.”
Personal loans and instant access savings accounts are the first two products under NatWest and Sainsbury’s long-term strategic partnership. The partnership will also see NatWest Retail provide a new NatWest Nectar credit card later this year.

title: European Banks Struggling to Catch Fraud at Instant Payment Speeds, Finds Sumsub
summary:
European banks, insurers, fintechs and other financial institutions are fighting increasingly sophisticated fraud with disconnected systems that can’t see the whole customer journey, according to new research from global verification and fraud prevention leader Sumsub. 
Sumsub's new report, The State of European Financial Services: 2026, finds that most firms run prevention and compliance processes through fragmented systems that can’t share data quickly enough to stop fraud in progress:
Only 9% of financial institutions run an integrated platform across fraud and compliance functions
18% have identity, fraud, payment and AML data fully integrated in real time
Nearly half of institutions say a quarter or more of alerts still require manual review
Detecting fraud earlier is the industry's top priority for the next 24 months (37%)
UK and Ireland lead Europe on integration but still catch fraud late
The UK and Ireland are the most advanced on joined-up systems: 13% of firms run an integrated fraud and compliance platform and over 1 in 5 (21%) have fully real-time data integration, both above the European average. Even so, fraud is still most often first caught at account access (41%) or payment initiation (37%), with only 17% of firms most commonly detecting fraud at onboarding, before fraudsters can do any serious damage.
Unauthorised payment fraud and impersonation fraud are the joint top fraud challenges (according to 33% of firms), with identity theft close behind (32%)
KYC is the biggest source of compliance pressure for almost half of firms (46%)
Detecting fraud earlier is the top priority for 41% of firms
Elsewhere in Europe, the gaps are wider. In DACH, just 8% of firms run an integrated platform and only 10% have fully real-time data integration, the lowest of all the regions surveyed. In France and Benelux, over one in four (26%) most commonly catch fraud only after a payment has settled, the highest share of any region.
Central Europe is the only region where detecting fraud earlier isn’t the top priority, with firms instead prioritising improving AML effectiveness (35%). This aligns with the region's wider compliance landscape: sanctions screening is its biggest source of compliance pressure (36%), and EU AML reform is the change expected to demand the most work (35%).
Fraud is largely being caught when the money is already moving 
The report finds only 17% of firms say fraud is first detected at onboarding, meaning that the fraudsters who pass those initial checks can move undetected between siloed systems until they’re ready to act. 
Fraud is more often first caught during account access (32%), payment initiation (29%) or withdrawal (29%). In nearly one in four cases (24%) fraudulent activity only comes to light after a customer complaint.
Regulation is forcing finance to move at a speed fraud teams can't match
Institutional pressure is being intensified by the EU's Instant Payments Regulation, which requires euro transfers to complete within ten seconds, leaving firms with far less time to stop a fraudulent transaction. Meanwhile, much of the industry still runs on manual review, often with limited workforces, leaving no margin for error at instant payment speeds.
Practitioners rank the Instant Payments Regulation (27%) and Verification of Payee (26%) above the EU AI Act (21%) and the EU AML Regulation (22%) as the developments forcing the greatest change over the next 24 months
One in three (32%) say slow investigations are their biggest operational weakness
Staff capacity is the biggest challenge in responding to regulatory change (36%), ahead of integrating new controls (34%) and budget (33%), meaning firms can’t simply hire their way out
Execs fear reputational damage more than fines
The top two biggest concerns for executives are reputational harm (42%) and criminal liability (37%), far outranking regulatory penalties (24%). A fine is a one-off cost that firms can absorb, but as reputational damage compounds, customers quickly lose faith. 
Customer churn ranks as the third-biggest fraud fear (31%). Unlike a fine, lost trust keeps costing the firm every time a would-be customer chooses a rival that appears safer.
Almost six in ten firms expect their fraud and compliance technology budgets to increase over the next 12 months, but the data suggests much of that spend will land on systems that are already fragmented. Nearly four in ten firms only have identity, fraud, payment and AML data partially integrated at best. The real-time capabilities that would close those gaps are stuck in pilot, with real-time decisioning more often partially deployed (36%) than fully live (29%). 
"European financial institutions are not short of fraud and compliance tools, but those tools don’t talk to each other," said Ilya Brovin, Chief Growth Officer at Sumsub. "Fraudsters exploit the gaps between siloed systems, and regulation is now demanding decisions in seconds that many firms still make in days. The case for a single view of the customer journey has moved from the operations team's agenda to the board's."
Sumsub's The State of European Financial Services: 2026 report is available to download here: https://sumsub.com/blog/guides-reports/the-state-of-european-financial-s...
NoYesPayments28 Sep, 2026
content: A new report from Sumsub reveals that European financial institutions are struggling to catch sophisticated fraud at instant payment speeds due to fragmented and disconnected systems. Most firms still rely on manual reviews and fail to share data quickly across compliance functions. With new regulations like the EU Instant Payments Regulation demanding rapid decisions, executives fear reputational damage and customer churn as fraud detection often happens too late.
